note: Both give the Cornell bookplate text and URL 'cu31924014590529' correctly; the differences are only in tags and image description.
Both have wrong readings, but X invents 'πόλεως τύχαι' where the print has 'πολυχρονίαν' and 'ἐν λοιδορήματι' for 'εὐλοιδόρητον'; Y garbles only the heading ('Ἐν τῷ σβίνε') and reads 'γὰρ αἰσχρὸν'.
Same text in both, but X misreads 'perpessæ' as 'perpetæ' and has the typo 'graviffimíſque'; Y matches the print.

X replaces printed phrases with invented ones ('ὅτου ἂν ἐπαγγελίῃσιν εἴδηται' for 'δεδειγμένων ἤδη τῶν τεχνέων'; 'οὐκ ἔστιν. εἴπερ ἰδέτω' for 'οὐκ εἴη … τοῦτο'; 'δὲ οὐχ ὃ' for 'οὐ τοῦτο'), though Y has its own slips ('ἀπορέω' for 'ἀποστερέω').
X leaves out the first Latin line, 'duobus electos audito modo; ut'; Y keeps it (Y's catchword 'τιο-' should be 'τεσ-').
X reads 'ἡ τετρὰς' where the print has 'τριάς', and 'ἑκάστῳ εἴδει τῶν πολυγώνων' for 'ἑκάστου εἴδους τοῦ πολυγώνου'; it also attaches stray Greek ('καὶ ἐπιπέδῳ') to the end of the Latin column.
The wording is identical in both and matches the page ('Let us once more, then, recall…'); they differ only in markup and line breaks.
X has 'πληρωμένοι' for 'πεπληρωμένοι' and the garbage token 'προσgrowthλώσας' for 'προσηλώσας'; Y is correct.
The text is the same in both, but X puts verse 13 at 'ζεταί' when the print places it at 'ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ', and reads the signature 'N ii' as 'N n'.
The text of Matt. 4:3–12 is the same in both; X moves some verse numbers (9 at 'Ταῦτα'), and the two read the first fragment differently ('γνάσε' / 'νωσε').
